answer.answer: Audit-ready takeover completed. The original import remains losslessly preserved, its version claim is corrected to the authoritative two-axis boundary, duplicated game data was not promoted into a competing snapshot, and rejected Flowworks work remains audit-only. Checkpoint committed as checkpoint:fb690b9a-00a6-9ccb-2a36-31ef24f16d8a.

claims.value: The preserved source is `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip`, supplied on 2026-07-11: 21,674,717 bytes, SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`, with 123 archive entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. `unzip -t` passed and every packaged SHA-256 passed. The original ZIP and verified extracted tree remain under ignored `raw/`; tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` retain the audit record. Preserved raw material includes the legacy SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script; recorded hashes include SQLite `d9ffbae20414d9e05a5dc02a664c904bc2bf0b8d74c8ae427ee9e8dccf6669fc`, snapshot JSON `373e0f0dc556ce9cc03120321356bf7ce85fc012ffd7b49ce1aac3e89e6abf59`, and workbook `2cb9f89360b9a721b2f41771ac77643a0438cb27e96b4f84a161ba93e7e04263`.

The archive retrieval time was `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`; its source-site version and reliable numeric-data build identity were not recorded. Its repeated attribution of numeric data to build `23761620` is therefore too strong: that was only the latest public executable observed. The correct two-axis boundary is (1) source/game data: Update 1, internal version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441`, with canonical SRDB `2.3.4` captured 2026-07-11 as snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`; versus (2) latest public executable observed at capture: Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`. Imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until rerun against that canonical snapshot.

No second canonical game-data snapshot was created. The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically duplicated by the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing snapshot. Unique material selectively promoted was `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`; explicit consumable-effect assumptions in `sources/consumable-effects.json`; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected two normalization defects: `airlock` had been overwritten by a building-shaped detail response, and Training Corporation retained a literal `$undefined` index.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is preserved only as superseded audit history; its buffer-minimization model, five-output-depot bank, and later overbuilt three-Stabilizer/two-slow-press direction must not become current guidance without new evidence. The authoritative July 11 staged Flowworks plan is an adopted plan, not confirmed construction: the level-10 cell uses one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps; the second Stabilizer is added before Scanner/levels 11–12; and one HRS v2 pad is reserved and built only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. The active RuptureOps pipeline/database and the current progression and operating-model notes remain authoritative over the preserved raw archive.

answer.answer: The three dumps are preserved losslessly but reconciled into one durable history. Dump 01 adds no conversation content; Dumps 02 and 03 contribute only their identified unique spans. Evidence classification prevents questions, assistant recommendations, accepted plans, and historical checkpoints from being promoted into current player facts. Canonical state is split among the installed-state model, machine-readable history, human-readable timeline, and evidence-derived product requirements.

claims.value: Dump 01 is a semantic-subset formatting variant: lines 1-226 reproduce the earlier factory-planning export with formatting differences and omitted attachment stanzas, so it adds no unique conversation content. Dump 02 substantially overlaps through lines 1-96 and contributes unique lines 99-249 covering the app origin, later-game scaling preferences, installed-state corrections, freight conventions, and Cargo Dispatcher ideas. Dump 03 substantially overlaps at lines 2-91, repeats the final export request at line 229, and contributes unique lines 95-225 covering the exploration pivot, Copperfield death, food observations, low-twitch combat constraint, and unresolved weapon/Yellowstone questions. All three raw sources remain preserved intact; they do not create another game-data snapshot or competing save versions.

Only direct first-person reports may support player state, history, preferences, and observations. Questions establish goals or uncertainty, not the truth of their premises; quoted assistant text remains recommendation rather than an independent player observation; accepted plans remain distinct from installed or completed save state; and hypotheses remain explicitly unproven. Thus proposed Flowworks, Grand Basin, and Cargo construction cannot become installed facts, and a suspected routing bug cannot become established causation without further evidence.

The dumps lack original timestamps and come from overlapping conversation branches, so chronology uses explicit narrative before/after ordering rather than a reconstructed dated log. Historical checkpoints do not silently overwrite current unknowns: persistent unlocks may remain likely, but current ownership, inventory, counts, progression, and construction require refreshed evidence. Repeated statements strengthen provenance while remaining one canonical fact; raw occurrences stay intact, but promotion is idempotent and does not multiply facts or create competing save snapshots.

The canonical promoted outputs are: `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json` for the best current installed-state model, with planned and confirmed construction separated; `models/rourke-update1-play-history__20260711.json` for machine-readable historical checkpoints, incidents, durable preferences, and unresolved state; `Player save - play history.md` for the canonical human-readable gameplay timeline; and `Player-derived product requirements.md` for translating direct play evidence into product requirements without declaring every idea an MVP feature. The earlier ZIP import remains canonical for its screenshots, generated reports, and more complete first factory-planning transcript.

answer.answer: Field brief: Little Cloud is manageable, but your pack is worth more than the time saved by gambling. Bank excess ammunition and consumables if storage is reasonably close; otherwise move methodically and leave replacement gear outside the tagged chamber’s failure domain. Starry Night is the easier site—clear any wanderers, take the final chest first, then loot debris.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Within 250 units it has 13 persistent hostile spawn entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers indicate possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers.

Because the player is carrying valuable ammunition and consumables, bank the excess first if storage is reasonably quick. Otherwise continue methodically, treating the nearby claimed Regeneration Chamber as useful travel insurance but keeping replacement equipment and a recovery cache outside its failure domain.

A claimed Regeneration Chamber does not protect carried equipment: Update 1 makes carried weapons losable on death. Field evidence also shows corruption disabling a contested base and its claimed chamber, after which the player respawned at the starting launcher. That encounter does not establish a universal corruption threshold or every condition governing chamber availability.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, although roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains the Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module; clear wanderers and open that chest before looting debris.

answer.answer: The first Geo Scanner lesson is now preserved as durable operational guidance: prepare both the defense and recovery path, while keeping the corruption mechanic and loot details within their actual evidence boundaries.

claims.value: The first Geo Scanner defense required three attempts. After the first death, the player respawned at a nearby claimed base that lacked replacement weapons and materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the second attempt, the temporary scanner fire base’s installed turrets were unpowered; the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and the next respawn occurred at the starting launcher. A third attempt then succeeded with a fully built-out fire base and all turrets powered.

The successful intervention was to fully build out the scanner fire base and power every turret before activation. The resulting automated defense completed the encounter and was a strongly positive payoff; the player described listening to the turrets “singing” against the enemy.

The failure chain and recovery are historical direct player observation. They demonstrate that, in this encounter, corruption disabled the temporary fire base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber after the player was overwhelmed. They do not establish a universal corruption threshold or every condition under which corruption disables Regeneration Chambers; those mechanics remain unverified beyond this incident.

For future Geo Scanner defenses: fully construct the fire base; power and function-check every turret before activation; stock the nearby recovery point with replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials; keep a safe cache outside the contested base’s corruption failure domain; and plan the worst-case respawn and return route. The completed site appeared to provide two unusually good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the dictated wording does not establish the item identities, whether these were items or stacks, or their exact counts. The completed scanner’s identity and coordinates are also unresolved.

answer.answer: Field checkpoint: launch from Faraday and preserve the three-outing order. Carry the full progression queue throughout; use defensive, low-twitch combat tactics and the Nutri Block/Chew food system. Historical save facts from 2026-07-11 require a live refresh before assuming current ownership or completion state.

claims.value: Recorded launch point: Faraday, immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn.” Route order: (1) use the Post-Rupture cave window, then Warm Dawn → Grey Owl → Lemon Souls → Purple Haze; (2) Little Cloud → Starry Night → optional scanner → Mythic Cry/Grand Basin, surveying rather than building if progression-gated; (3) make the Forgotten Engine the third focused outing—full fog clearing is not a prerequisite. Run Redleaf afterward only if its Turbine/Electromagnetic Coil blueprint package remains the blocker.

Keep the complete simultaneous queue active: unlock blueprints; reveal more of the map; gather Quartz; permanently solve food; earn War Bonds for the Machine Gun; assess and prepare for the Forgotten Engine; later establish Goethite and Oil supply; and keep directions grounded in the player’s named geography. At the recorded checkpoint, the Forgotten Engine was not confirmed complete, the Machine Gun was not yet unlocked, and Goethite/Oil supply was not established; all require live-state refresh.

The player is explicitly poor at twitch FPS play, so operate defensively: shotgun for close waves/corridors and an accurate rifle for Flingers, Spitters, and controlled ranged fire; favor doors, cover, line-of-sight breaks, shields, retreats, a manual-save safety point, and a preserved abort route. Stage ammunition and healing before entry and never depend on cross-planet live ammunition delivery during combat. Do not casually trigger high-threat sites: accidental Copperfield aggro exhausted ammunition, prevented escape, and ended in death. SLAMS-12, MAR-9, M175, LEM, and mod suggestions are recommendations—not confirmed inventory; current weapons, mods, ammunition, Power Cell state, Machine Gun unlock, and blueprint ownership remain unknown until refreshed.

Permanent low-chore system: Polufruit → Calorie Chew, Hydrobulb → Aqua Chew, Prickler → Nutri Block, Glowcap → medicine. Before departure, refill with 3 Calorie Chews + 1 Aqua Chew (use 2 existing Hydrolites instead of the Aqua Chew while they last), take 1 Nutri Block, carry 2 Blocks per planned hour + 2 spares, and carry one complete Chew refill; double the Chew backup for a very long trip. Do not use Purfins, Antidote Gel, or another effect-stripping item while a Block is active. Carry 5–10 Glowcaps for ordinary combat or 25–40 for the Forgotten Engine, and bank every cave Glowcap. Gather Prickler first, Polufruit second, and convenient Oxallop next; 58 additional Prickler completes the recorded first target of 20 Blocks/10 hours. Rebuild buffers at 20 minimum/40 comfortable Nutri Blocks, 30/60 Calorie Chews, and 10 Aqua Chews after Hydrolites are depleted. Figler and routine Hydrolite/Nutri Gel replenishment are rejected as high-chore or bottleneck-wasting.

answer.answer: The resumed Watch Session design is an evidence-backed proposal, not a verified implementation. claims.value: Version 1 was created and updated 2026-07-11. The 54-minute fire-wave-impact-to-impact cycle is strongly corroborated by starrupture.tools and an independent runtime-reading mod, but Creepy Jar has published no numerical phase formula; it must remain a versioned community/game-data model. Internal warning boundaries and opportunity transitions still require live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation, so use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat—not exact, safe, or guaranteed—and do not invent numerical accuracy.

claims.value: Expose five player-meaningful states while retaining the 54-minute model: Fire wave 0:00-0:30, Cooling 0:30-1:30, Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30, World active 11:30-51:30, and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00. Manual synchronization anchors 0:00 when the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait hierarchy, visible without scrolling, is: sync/capability line; semantic hero state and across-the-room monospaced countdown; explicit countdown target; threat instruction and one action sentence; at most two opportunity cards; then exact-time next events with Mute one cycle and Re-sync. During recovery, the hero target is expected ordinary-Vermin return; during normal ecology, it is the next Ruptura or warning phase. Retain a proportional overview, but add minimum-width labeled steps or next events so short phases never collapse visually.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are independently versioned evidence records, not phase mechanics. Each OpportunityWindow carries an ID, start and end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Initial guidance includes reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery with triggered-encounter caveats; early-recovery dry-lakebed Oxallop; favorable but non-guaranteed cave access, Quartz, and Glowcaps; post-cooling/recovery Ignitium with variable spawn rate; experimental late-recovery Star Tears tied to leaving cooled Ignitium unharvested; variable post-wave Coralion/Vulpir eggs; non-exact regrowth wording for foliage and water; and hidden Sulheart guidance until timing is validated. The UI should show at most two prioritized cards with provenance and explicitly present the Ignitium-versus-Star-Tears choice.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Enemy return and Ruptura require distinct visual, sound, and haptic signatures; never rely on color or audio alone. Enemy-return defaults escalate at 5 minutes, 2 minutes, 1 minute, 15 seconds, and the event; pre-Ruptura cues may occur at 10 minutes, 5 minutes, 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Support an exit buffer, Full/Haptic only/Visual only profiles, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, previews, Mute one cycle, and collapse missed cues after resume to the strongest current message rather than replaying a backlog. Confidence states are Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required; downgrade after correction, clock or model change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop. Store absolute timestamps, recompute from (now - anchor) modulo cycle duration, reschedule notifications after anchor/model/policy changes, and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Disable the idle timer only while monitoring and restore it; do not use background audio as keep-alive. Limit Live Activity to the armed event. AlarmKit requires explicit player arming and authorization—never silently schedule endless 54-minute alarms; older iOS uses normal notifications, Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Always pair color with text, symbols, borders, or patterns; support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion; avoid flashing transitions, default ticking, and per-second VoiceOver announcements; keep Re-sync, Mute one cycle, capabilities, and the next alert time visible.

answer.answer: RuptureOps is not ready for corpus-backed public distribution. A public build may currently use only a clean, source-free implementation shell with original code and independently licensed or platform-provided assets. It must exclude the existing data corpus, imports, personalized artifacts, mirrored images, generated icon, and warning audio until the relevant rights are established.

claims.value: The SRDB-derived source corpus remains private. Although robots.txt permits crawling, the SRDB footer asserts copyright and no explicit content/data reuse license is published. The private boundary includes captured RSC/static payloads, normalized datasets, the derived SQLite database, and all 1,081 indexed asset references—including 466 available logical assets represented by 454 unique privately mirrored blobs. Crawling permission is not republication permission, so neither the mirrored dataset nor its images/assets may be shipped publicly now.

All personalized imports and player-derived artifacts remain private: the three user-authored prompt-history dumps classified as private_player_context (58,207 bytes, 704 POSIX lines, 10,396 words, and 116 prompt delimiters); player save baselines and play-history models; player-specific planning notes; site/geography screenshots and assets; conversation-derived decisions; and the raw Star Rupture Game Analysis package. That package also contains a duplicate third-party corpus, generated binaries, a legacy SQLite database, personalized save context, and nine player-specific site/geography assets. Only tracked manifests and explicitly promoted, provenance-labeled facts belong in version control; this does not grant public redistribution rights.

The safe public-build boundary now is a clean, source-free unofficial application shell containing only original implementation and independently licensed or platform-provided assets. It must not bundle the normalized or raw data corpus, derived database, imports, player/save artifacts, site or player images, mirrored source icons, the generated app icon, or warning audio from this private fixture. Mission Timeline is the selected design direction, but the frozen evidence explicitly does not establish that the simulator/install-ready acceptance condition passed, so implementation readiness must not be overstated. The app must not imply Creepy Jar endorsement, and hidden, prototype, or stale play-test content must remain outside player-facing defaults.

Broader distribution requires either separate written reuse permission from the SRDB/source owner or replacement of the corpus with a different, separately licensed or first-party-permitted data strategy. After choosing that path, RuptureOps must perform asset-by-asset provenance and license clearance for images, icons, and audio; exclude personalized material; keep the product explicitly unofficial; preserve attribution and material version boundaries; and verify the resulting clean build before release. Until then, the repository and normalized corpus must remain private and must not be pushed to a public remote.
